Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Seattle WA
316 AM PST Tue Nov 17 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Split flow aloft over Western Washington today. Flow aloft
consolidating tonight with a weather system approaching the
coast. The system will move by to the south and weaken Wednesday
and Wednesday night. High amplitude upper level ridge building 
offshore Thursday with dry northerly flow aloft developing by 
Thursday night. Ridge moves over the area Friday before getting 
pinched off Friday night. Next system stalling off the coast 
over the weekend. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Satellite imagery shows mostly cloudy skies over Western
Washington early this morning. Doppler radar has some last gasp
showers along the coast. Fog has formed over the Southwest
Interior and along the Kitsap peninsula with visibilities below
a mile in some locations. Temperatures at 3 AM/11Z were in the 
mid 30s to lower 40s.

Split flow aloft over Western Washington today as the next
weather system approaches the area well offshore. Residual 
moisture left behind from the upper level trough that moved 
through Monday evening will be tough to get rid of this morning 
without any ridge building over the area. The layer is shallow 
so by afternoon expect less cloud cover and fog and more 
sunshine. Highs near 50.

Mostly clear skies tonight with the next system moving southeast
offshore. Clear skies and light flow over the interior lowlands
leading to more fog especially south of Seattle. Freezing fog 
possible over the Southwest Interior with low temperatures near 
freezing. Lows elsewhere in the mid 30s to lower 40s. Low level 
offshore flow increasing in the foothills with the cross cascade
gradient down to minus 6 to 8 mb by 12Z Wednesday. Increasing 
easterly winds in the foothills.

Cloud cover increasing quickly Wednesday morning as the next
system begins to move inland well south of the area. Bands of
showers rotating around the upper level low moving over
Southern Washington could get as far north as Everett during 
the day. Breezy east winds continuing in the foothills. Highs 
near 50. 

Upper level low weakening over Oregon Wednesday night into
Thursday. High amplitude upper level ridge building offshore
Thursday extending north into the Yukon. Dry northerly flow
aloft developing over Western Washington decreasing cloud cover
by Thursday afternoon. Lows in the mid 30s to lower 40s. Highs 
near 50. 

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY NIGHT THROUGH MONDAY/...
Models in good agreement Thursday night into Friday with the
high amplitude upper level ridge offshore moving over Western 
Washington Friday. Ridge gets pinched off Friday night as 
another system sets off off the coast. Models still having 
trouble coming to a consistent solution over the weekend. Some 
ensemble solutions take the system offshore and move it inland 
south of the area Saturday night into Sunday. Other ensemble 
solutions stall the system off the Washington coast. With a lack
of a consensus will stay with the chance of rain forecast over 
the weekend. Snow levels around 2500 feet so any precipitation 
the Cascades get will be in the form of snow in the passes. 

Inconsistencies in the solutions continue into Monday with a
pair of possible solutions the leading contenders, one an upper
level ridge building over the area and two what is left of the 
stalled system offshore moving through Western Washington. 
Ensemble solutions are no help keeping the broadbrush chance of 
rain forecast going into Monday. Snow levels remaining below 
pass levels.

Lows in the upper 20s and 30s Friday and Saturday morning, mid
30s to lower 40s Sunday and Monday morning. Highs near 50 
through the period. Felton

&&

.AVIATION...
A mix of conditions ranging from VFR to LIFR with low clouds and fog 
over the region this morning. Fog has developed over the southern 
interior and Kitsap Peninsula with conditions deteriorating to LIFR. 
For locations that remain VFR, latest satellite imagery shows low 
clouds trying to fill in over the interior terminals and may bring 
MVFR cigs this morning. Terminal-wide VFR expected this afternoon 
after 17Z-20Z with fog/clouds scattering out. Guidance hints at 
another round of fog and low clouds possible Wednesday morning. 
Southeasterly winds this afternoon will transition southwesterly. 
Winds will transition northeasterly Tuesday evening, with easterly 
winds increasing Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, particularly 
through the Cascade gaps, Strait of Juan de Fuca, and HQM.  

KSEA...VFR today. Fog will develop near the terminal this morning, 
but not expected to impact the terminal. Rather low clouds may 
materialize between 12Z-17Z, with a 25-30% chance of MVFR cigs. 
Chances for IFR still remain around 10% or less. Southeasterly winds 
will transition southwesterly this afternoon around 5 kt. Winds will 
transition northeasterly this evening around 00Z, increasing to 6-9 
kt. 

29

&&

.MARINE...
Winds expected to increase across the waters today and will turn 
offshore this evening as a low pressure system offshore moves 
southwards across the NE Pacific. Additionally, offshore winds will 
be locally enhanced along terrain gaps, particularly through the 
Strait of Juan de Fuca and near Grays Harbor Tuesday night. Small 
Craft Advisories have been issued for the West and Central Strait of 
Juan de Fuca, with latest high-res guidance indicating a 70-100% 
chance of small craft winds. Winds across the outer coastal waters 
expected to reach gale thresholds this afternoon, for which a Gale 
Warning has been issued. Gusts may also briefly reach gale along the 
inner coastal waters Wednesday morning at times, especially the 
waters adjacent to the West Entrance of the Strait of Juan de Fuca 
and Grays Harbor County. As of this morning, the Small Craft 
Advisory for the inner coastal waters has been extended through 
Wednesday morning. Seas will briefly decrease to 10 feet or below 
this afternoon, before increasing to to 10-15 feet Tuesday night 
into Wednesday. 

As the low pressure system continues to push south into California 
and away from area waters, weak high pressure will build late 
Wednesday into Thursday for calmer marine conditions. An active 
weather pattern returns  this weekend into next week as multiple 
systems are expected to move over the waters.
